title: Kenyan Mango Juice
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Mango Juice — ripe Kenyan mangoes blended smooth, diluted to the perfect consistency, and lightly sweetened. Kenya grows some of the finest mangoes in the world — when they are in season, this juice is extraordinary.
longDesc: Kenya produces over 20 commercial mango varieties, from the Kent and Apple mangoes of the coast to the Ngowe of the Rift Valley and the Tommy Atkins of Central Kenya. When mangoes are in season, every roadside stall overflows with them, and fresh mango juice — thick, sweet, and intensely fruity — is available on every corner. It is arguably the finest fruit juice Kenya produces.
ingredients: 4 large ripe mangoes — peeled and diced
1—2 tbsp sugar — if mangoes need it
1 tbsp lime or lemon juice — optional

substitutions.alternative: Frozen mango chunks — works well outside of mango season

steps: Peel and dice the mangoes, removing all flesh from the stone.
Blend the mango flesh with 1 cup of water until completely smooth.
Add remaining water to reach desired consistency — thicker is better for fresh mango juice.
Strain through a fine mesh strainer for a smooth juice (or skip straining for a mango nectar).
Add sugar only if needed — ripe mangoes may need none.
Add lime juice and pinch of salt.
chefTips: Use the ripest, most fragrant mangoes available — the quality of the mango is everything.
Keep it thick — Kenyan mango juice should have body, not be watery.
A squeeze of lime balances the sweetness and sharpens the tropical flavour.
commonMistakes: Under-ripe mangoes — the juice is tart and lacks the characteristic sweetness.
Too much water — dilutes the glorious mango flavour.

faqs.q: Which Kenyan mango variety is best for juice?
faqs.a: Apple mangoes and Kent mangoes have the best juice yield and flavour. Ngowe mangoes are extremely sweet and fragrant but have more fibre. Any fully ripe mango works beautifully.

cookingScience: Ripe mango flesh contains primarily sucrose, fructose, and glucose, plus over 300 identified aroma compounds including terpenes that give mango its characteristic tropical fragrance. The fully ripe fruit has the highest sugar content and most developed aroma profile — which is why ripeness is the most important factor in mango juice.
sustainabilityTips: Buy from local Kenyan mango farmers during peak season (October—February).
Mango peels and stones can be composted.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 2 days. Drink fresh for the best flavour.
healthBenefits: Rich in vitamin C and vitamin A (from beta-carotene).
Good source of folate and vitamin B6.
Naturally energising from natural fruit sugars.
culturalNote: Mango season in Kenya is a celebration in itself — the markets overflow with mangoes at every price point, and fresh mango juice becomes one of the most anticipated seasonal drinks. The variety and quality of Kenyan mangoes is genuinely world-class.
regionalVariations: Mango and passion fruit blend — the most popular combination.
